leading_positions.synthesis: Three members put magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene in their round-1 configuration, each with Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Bistritzer, and each citing a prediction of flat bands at a magic angle followed by the 2018 discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. Mehlig moved to it from his own first choice B009 after reading the opening ballots. They share the view that the prize criterion is a discovery, not a settled explanation, so the unresolved superconducting mechanism should not by itself block it, and that the citation should be worded around the prediction and the observed phases. They differ in emphasis: Danielsson stresses breadth of the field created, Olsson stresses that twist angle and local structure are directly checkable and asks that the pre-2018 moire band-structure literature be checked before wording is fixed, and Mehlig stresses the single tunable control parameter. All three concede that B012 is the more mature alternative, and all list it as a first alternative. Non-supporters who raised this candidate (Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Pearce) object mainly on maturity of interpretation and, for Eriksson, on whether Bistritzer is as decisive as the other two.

Two members put the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulator (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) in their round-1 configuration. Johansson moved to it from circuit QED (B004), which he ranked first in the opening ballot and now advises he should not carry weight on or decide; Pearce moved to it from B031, which drew no other support. Both rely on its breadth in the opening ballots (seven of eight members ranked it, all between second and fourth, and all seven proposed the same trio) and on more than fifteen years of confirmation by transport, ARPES and STM. Both flag the same weakness: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (the HgTe prediction; Zhang is deceased) and the 3D topological-insulator contributors are outside the credited names, and the 2016 prize on topological phases is a possible overlap. The two citations differ slightly in wording of the experimental part (observation versus first observation in HgTe quantum wells). B012 also appears as a listed alternative for six other members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson), but that is not a statement that it is their preferred configuration.

Two members put the optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) in their round-1 configuration, with near-identical citations resting on magic-wavelength trapping and 10^-18 fractional uncertainty. They share the view that this has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, is demonstrated by several independent laboratories, and has measurable impact (fundamental-constant tests, millimetre-scale redshift). They also share the same reservations: possible overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, a still-pending redefinition of the second, and contributors such as Lemonde outside the two names. Kroll discloses an indirect connection (a research stay in John Hall's laboratory, Hall being Ye's mentor) and Lindroth discloses adjacency as an atomic theorist. B019 is a listed alternative for Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce, who consider it strong but narrower in scientific reach or tied to a pending prospective milestone.

One member, Eriksson, keeps dynamical mean-field theory (Georges, Kotliar, Vollhardt) in his configuration, with reduced certainty and an explicit statement that his ranking is not evidence of consensus. He discloses a methodological and field-proximity bias. Colleagues who ranked it (Lindroth third, Mehlig sixth, Johansson seventh) accept its importance but object that it is a method and not a discovery, and that Metzner, Muller-Hartmann and Jarrell are outside the credited trio. Eriksson himself concedes that the attribution objection cannot be fully answered and invites the committee to look elsewhere if no fair three-name prize exists.

areas_of_agreement: The three most-supported configurations (B047, B012, B019) are each described by their own proponents as scientifically strong, reproduced by independent groups, and consistent with the discovery criterion; no member argues that any of them is not real physics.

B012 is the broadest point of overlap: seven of eight members ranked it in the opening round, all proposed the same trio, and six members list it as an alternative even where it is not their preferred configuration.
Most members treat B019 as having the cleanest attribution (two names, no serious competing claim to the core idea) and B047 as having the clearest prediction-then-discovery chain.

Several members agree that the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits weighs against circuit QED (B004) this year, and Johansson, who ranked B004 first at opening, advises that he should not carry weight on it.
Members broadly agree that a prize for B047 would be about the prediction and observed phases, not about the superconducting mechanism, and that the citation wording would need to reflect that.

Active-matter hydrodynamics (B009) and gamma-ray burst afterglows (B031) were each ranked first by a single member in the opening round and are no longer in the preferred configuration or alternatives of their original advocates (Mehlig moved to B047, Pearce to B012; Mehlig still lists B009 as an alternative).
scientific_disputes: Whether the discovery in B047 is the existence of flat-band-driven correlated phases (Danielsson, Mehlig, Olsson) or whether the physical meaning of the superconducting and correlated states is too unsettled for a prize (Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Pearce).

Whether B012 is a distinct discovery from the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and topological phases (Pearce, Johansson argue the Z2 invariant and time-reversal-protected edge states came later and were separately verified; Danielsson, Eriksson and Pearce all list the overlap as an open question).

Whether the optical lattice clock (B019) is a new principle (parallel interrogation of many atoms with the lattice light shift cancelled, per Kroll and Lindroth) or a continuation of the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and whether it is narrower in scientific reach than moire matter or topological phases (Danielsson, Mehlig, Pearce).

Whether a theoretical framework or method such as DMFT (B005) fits the discovery criterion, with Eriksson pointing to spectroscopy and Mott-transition thermodynamics as experimental tests and Johansson, Olsson and Kroll doubting that usefulness equals discovery.

Whether the quantitative experimental tests of the Toner-Tu exponents in B009 are strong enough relative to the tests of B012 (raised by Danielsson, Johansson, Lindroth, Pearce in response to Mehlig).
attribution_disputes: B012: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction (Zhang deceased) and the 3D topological-insulator contributors (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hsieh, Hasan) are outside the credited Kane, Mele, Molenkamp trio; Pearce and Johansson argue Kane and Mele made the foundational proposal, while Mehlig and Lindroth call the omission a serious problem.

B047: Eriksson would credit only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, while Danielsson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce proposed Bistritzer as well because the 2011 continuum model first identified the magic angle; experimental first authors (Cao, Fatemi) and parallel moire work (Dean and colleagues) fall outside any three-name list, and Olsson asks for the pre-2018 moire band-structure literature to be checked.

B005: Metzner, Muller-Hartmann and Jarrell fall outside the credited Georges, Kotliar, Vollhardt trio, and Eriksson himself has not verified the priority split between the infinite-dimension limit and the impurity-model mapping.

B019: Lemonde (SYRTE) and other early lattice-clock proposers or groups, plus theorists of the magic-wavelength shift, fall outside the Katori and Ye pair; Kroll and Lindroth take priority details from memory and ask for them to be checked against the record.

B004: Devoret, Girvin and Koch (transmon and the 2004 proposal) cannot be accommodated by the credited Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf trio, per Kroll and Lindroth; no member currently carries B004 in a preferred configuration.
B009: Tu, a co-author of the continuum theory, is outside the credited Toner, Ramaswamy, Vicsek set (Lindroth, Pearce).
maturity_disputes: B047 is about eight years old; its supporters (Danielsson, Mehlig, Olsson) say reproduction across many laboratories and platforms suffices, while Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Pearce point to unsettled mechanism and twist-angle disorder limiting quantitative comparison with theory.

B012 is the most mature candidate by the account of its supporters and of the B047 supporters, with more than fifteen years of confirmation; the open question is whether that maturity outweighs the attribution gaps and the 2016 overlap.

B019: the redefinition of the second is still pending; Kroll and Lindroth treat the demonstrated 10^-18 performance across several laboratories as sufficient, while Danielsson, Mehlig, Johansson and Pearce treat part of the impact as prospective.
Johansson and Mehlig ask whether B047 could overtake B012 within a few years; Danielsson asks whether B012's broader opening support should discount B047.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers; directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology) discloses that circuit QED (B004) is his own field, names Chalmers colleagues Delsing, Wilson and Kockum, and advises that he should not carry weight on B004 and be recused from any decision on it; B004 is not in his configuration or alternatives.
Kroll discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory; Hall is Jun Ye's mentor, an indirect scientific connection to B019, and he would accept recusal discussion on that part.

Eriksson discloses a methodological and field-proximity bias for B005 (works with density functional theory and dynamical mean-field methods) and raises a possible recusal question if the committee thinks it amounts to a conflict.

Lindroth discloses adjacency as a theoretical atomic physicist for B019 and says collaborations with L'Huillier's and Keller's groups would require disclosure and possible recusal if attosecond science or highly charged ions were considered.
Mehlig discloses that his research on active matter is close to B009 (field proximity, not a personal tie).

Pearce (chair) discloses that B031, which he ranked first at opening, is close to his gamma-ray and hard-X-ray instrumentation work (Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur); he has not included B031 in his configuration or alternatives, and no conflict is apparent for B012, B047 or B019.

Olsson notes her Chalmers affiliation and colleague Johansson for completeness, with no documented tie to any credited name; Danielsson notes only that as a theorist he may favour candidates built on a decisive prediction.
questions_for_round2: B012: can a fair citation be drafted around Kane, Mele and Molenkamp that acknowledges the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction and the 3D topological-insulator work, or does the three-name limit make the attribution unfair? Is the 2016 prize a bar or only a context?

B047: should the committee treat the unsettled superconducting mechanism as a maturity bar or as a follow-up question, and can a citation be worded around the prediction and the observed correlated phases alone? If it can, is Bistritzer's inclusion warranted, and how should the experimental credit of Cao, Fatemi and others be handled?

B047 versus B012: given that B047's supporters list B012 as the more mature alternative and B012's supporters list B047 as a first alternative, is the choice about this year or about a later year, and what evidence would change members' ordering?

B019: is the lattice clock a new discovery or invention distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and is the pending redefinition of the second a reason to wait or already satisfied by demonstrated 10^-18 performance? Please verify the priority history between Katori, Ye and Lemonde.

Should B004 receive any weight this year, given the 2025 superconducting-circuits prize, the unresolved Devoret, Girvin, Koch credit, and Johansson's recusal advice? Are B005, B009, B031 and B017 to be treated as live configurations by any member in round 2?

Does any member prefer a multi-part prize combining two candidates (for example B047 with B012 or B019), and if so on what grounds of fields and shares, given that every round-1 configuration is a single part?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows three single-part preferred configurations with explicit support (B047 by three members, B012 by two, B019 by two), and one (B005) by one member. Support is not a ruling: B012 has the broadest opening ranking and appears as an alternative for six members, while B047 has the most explicit supporters in this round, and the disputes concentrate on maturity of interpretation for B047, attribution for B012, and novelty against earlier prizes for B019. All explicit counts here come only from the eight round-1 files, and several members changed their preferred configuration after the opening round, so positions remain fluid going into round 2.
